steps.message:
Gordon, Bianca at Ocotillo wants a straight answer on whether the E119 companion simulation validated, for the launch materials. I can't close my review of the Phase 1 draft until section 7 exists, so I need the validation memo from you.

Work from the companion run as it stands, the appropriate test report and certification document, the amended numbers Bianca sent over, and the dimensioned assembly drawing. Our own procedure governs how the result gets reported. No new runs or tests are available and nothing is being asked of Red Butte or Ironwood, so this comes out of what is on the file server today, 10/10/2025, and nothing else on it needs changing.

Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on. I need the governing criterion and the time it is reached, and I need to know whether the prediction in the section 7 stub stands. I need the experimental value you adopt and your disposition on Bianca's figure. On the strength of those I need the error, the acceptance criterion, the uncertainty, and how the error compares against both. I also want the largest prediction that would have cleared the criterion.

Two comparisons belong in the memo as well: the minutes separating the two criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and how far the governing point sits above the nine point mean at governance in each. Tell me what they say about the model, where the rework belongs, and whether any of that rework has been started yet. I also need what all of this means for the rest of Phase 1.

The memo also needs what this exercise does and does not establish about Ocotillo's wildfire claim and what would close that gap, including the form any future comparison would have to be reported in. I need what Bianca's figure would do to the certified rating if it were ever substantiated and who is entitled to act on that, the stamp language, and my checklist disposition: which item the memo lets me close and which of the rest stay open. Give it to me as a Word memo with crossing times rather than the samples that trip them, times to the nearest minute, limits as they fall, and every number carrying its unit. Add a short paragraph I can send Bianca today.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

1. TEST STANDARD AND METHOD
The evaluation reported here was performed in accordance with ASTM E119, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests
of Building Construction and Materials (current edition). One vertical fire-endurance test was performed on the wall
assembly described in Section 2, using the standard time-temperature curve prescribed by ASTM E119. The
exposed face of the assembly was subjected to the E119 standard curve delivered by the laboratory's natural-gas
vertical wall furnace, with furnace temperatures monitored by nine furnace thermocouples symmetrically distributed
on the exposed face per the standard.
The assembly was tested as a non-load-bearing partition. The applicable fire-endurance criteria for a
non-load-bearing wall under ASTM E119 are the following two thermal-transmission conditions on the unexposed
face:

• Average unexposed-face criterion. The average temperature rise measured by nine thermocouples
symmetrically disposed on the unexposed face of the specimen shall not exceed 139 degC (250 degF) above the
initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.

• Single-point criterion. The temperature rise at any single thermocouple on the unexposed face shall not exceed
181 degC (325 degF) above the initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.
Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two thermal-transmission criteria governs the reported fire endurance for the
specimen.

2. SPECIMEN DESCRIPTION
One 3.05 m × 3.05 m (10 ft × 10 ft) specimen was constructed by the client at the Red Butte laboratory prior to test.
The specimen is a double-wythe 3D-printed concrete wall assembly consisting of two printed concrete leaves
separated by an open-air cavity and connected by continuous truss-type steel ties.

2.1 Concrete leaves
• Number of leaves: two, oriented parallel and in registration.
• Leaf thickness: each leaf 50 mm as printed and cured (siliceous aggregate mix).
• Aggregate: siliceous.
• Placement: wet-on-wet extruded 3D printing; nominal 20 mm bead pitch; leaves printed vertically on the
specimen frame and cured to the manufacturer's 28-day protocol prior to shipment for test.

2.2 Cavity

 • Cavity width: 205 mm between the interior surfaces of the two leaves.

2. Governing Endurance Result
ASTM E119 was applied to the specimen described in Section 1.2 above. Two thermal-transmission criteria apply to
a non-load-bearing wall under ASTM E119, and the earlier of the two governs the reported fire endurance:

• Average unexposed-face criterion — the nine-thermocouple mean rise shall not exceed 139 °C above initial
ambient. Per Section 5.1 of the Red Butte test report, the average criterion was reached at 163 min after test
start.

• Single-point criterion — the rise at any single thermocouple on the unexposed face shall not exceed 181 °C
above initial ambient. Per Section 5.2 of the Red Butte test report, the single-point criterion was reached at 118
min after test start at thermocouple 6, which was positioned directly opposite a horizontal course of the 3.8 mm
truss-type steel wall ties described in Section 1.2 above.

 Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two criteria governs the reported fire endurance. The single-point criterion was
reached first, and therefore the measured fire endurance of the assembly is 118 min.
The single-point governance at thermocouple 6 is consistent with the presence of the continuous steel tie course as a
metallic thermal-bridge path between the exposed and unexposed leaves at that location. The average
unexposed-face temperature rise across the remaining eight thermocouples did not approach the single-point
criterion at the moment of governance and is a distinct and later-occurring result, as documented in Section 5 of the
Red Butte test report.

3. Certification
On the basis of the certified test identified in Section 1.1 and the governing endurance result stated in Section 2,
Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering certifies the assembly for a 1-hour fire-resistance rating (60 min).
The measured endurance of 118 min exceeds the 60-minute rung by a healthy margin. The next higher standard rung
is a 2-hour rating, which requires 120 min of demonstrated endurance under the governing criterion; the measured
endurance falls short of that rung by 2 min. Because the certified rating is limited by the governing single-point result
to the highest standard rung fully demonstrated by the certified test, the assembly is certified at 1-hour and not at any
higher rung.

and 1.3. It is not a statement about any other assembly, any other configuration of ties, cavity contents, leaf
thickness, or aggregate, or any other fire exposure than the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve.

4. Amendments and Reissuance
Any change to the certified rating requires a reissued test report from the testing laboratory of record and a new
certification issued by Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering. No other party may certify or restate this rating.

5. Limitations
5.1 Standard exposure only. The certified rating is a comparative assembly rating derived from performance under
the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve as delivered by a laboratory furnace. It is a measure of the
thermal-transmission behavior of the specific assembly described in Section 1.2 under a standard fire exposure.
5.2 Not a wildfire-performance statement. The ASTM E119 exposure is a standardized post-flashover
compartment-fire curve. It is not representative of a wildland-urban-interface (WUI) wildfire exposure, which involves
radiant and convective heat loading from an advancing vegetation fire, a distinct heat-flux history, wind-driven flame
tilt, and firebrand deposition, among other phenomena not present in the E119 furnace test. Nothing in this
certification should be read as a WUI wildfire survival prediction for the assembly, the structures in which the
assembly is installed, or the occupants of those structures.
5.3 Non-load-bearing configuration. The assembly was tested and is certified in a non-load-bearing configuration
only. Loaded configurations require a separate load-bearing test and a separate certification.
5.4 No hose-stream criterion. No hose-stream retest was contracted or performed. Where a jurisdiction or code
requires a hose-stream criterion in addition to thermal transmission, that requirement is not addressed by this
certification.
5.5 As-built conformance. This certification presupposes that the assembly installed in the field conforms to the
geometry and materials described in Section 1.2. Field verification of conformance is the responsibility of the design
and construction team of record for each installation.
